text:
Macklin Celebrini is playing career-high minutes, and Sharks Hockey Digest put it plainly: "It's Not Sustainable, But Sharks Need It Right Now." The numbers say the same. His line with Will Smith and Igor Chernyshov takes 62 percent of the expected goals (the quality of the chances) and has outscored opponents 4-2, but Celebrini has 7 points in his last 10 games when his chances say about 13.6. He's due some puck luck, and so is the team.

San Jose is 8-11-1 with 17 points and finally snapped a five-game skid on Monday, with Ivar Stenberg winning a 3-2 shootout over the Islanders. The underlying problem is in their own end: they allow 3.94 expected goals per 60 minutes, and take 43 percent of the expected goals overall. The goalies have helped, allowing about 10 fewer goals than expected; the shooters haven't, scoring 11.54 fewer than their chances deserve. Those two gaps roughly cancel out.

The rookies are learning in public. The line of Kiefer Sherwood, Michael Misa and Stenberg has only 34 percent of the expected goals. On defense, Darnell Nurse and Michael Kesselring have been outscored 3-12 together. Our simulations give the Sharks a 4 percent playoff chance. The thing to watch is the minutes: whether the young players can take enough of them that Celebrini doesn't have to.
headline: Celebrini is carrying more than he can
